title: Melting phase diagram of the two-dimensional electron solid in a perpendicular magnetic field
authors: M. Yu. Melnikov, D. G. Smirnov, A. A. Shashkin, S. -H. Huang, C. ~W. Liu, S. V. Kravchenko
abstract: We determine the thermal melting phase diagram of the electron solid by measuring the onset density of the double-threshold voltage-current curves in the insulating state in the ultra-high mobility two-dimensional electron system in SiGe/Si/SiGe quantum wells at different temperatures in perpendicular magnetic fields. The introduction of a magnetic field leads to a considerable increase in the onset density, which is strongest at the lowest temperatures and decreases with increasing temperature, and the melting temperature increases with magnetic field. These data are in agreement with theoretical predictions. Unexpectedly, the melting temperature as a function of electron density in a fixed magnetic field reveals a plateau, which can be interpreted in terms of resonance modes in the crystallites.
summary: This work experimentally maps the thermal melting phase diagram of a 2D electron solid in a perpendicular magnetic field. By analyzing voltage-current characteristics, the researchers confirm that the magnetic field stabilizes the solid phase. Most notably, they observe a plateau in the melting temperature versus density curve, which they interpret as evidence of resonance modes within the crystalline structure.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the thermal melting phase diagram of a two-dimensional electron solid.
main_result: The magnetic field increases the melting temperature, and the melting temperature exhibits an unexpected plateau as a function of electron density, which is attributed to resonance modes in the crystallites.
method: Measurements involve analyzing the onset density of double-threshold voltage-current (I-V) curves in the insulating state of a 2D electron system.
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-dimensional electron system confined in SiGe/Si/SiGe quantum wells, which is studied under perpendicular magnetic fields. The theoretical framework involves modeling the electron solid, potentially as a Wigner crystal.
key_observables: Onset density of double-threshold V-I curves, melting temperature ($T_c$), and the dependence of $T_c$ on magnetic field and electron density.
important_parameters: Temperature (T), perpendicular magnetic field (B), and electron density ($n_s$).
main_assumptions: The analysis adapts a phenomenological theory of the collective depinning of elastic structures, and the plateau is interpreted via resonance modes in the crystallites.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows typical V-I characteristics at different temperatures and densities, illustrating the two-threshold behavior. Figure 2 shows the melting temperature ($T_c$) dependence on electron density, highlighting the plateau region.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical system and the diagnostic tool (double-threshold V-I curves). It presents results showing magnetic field dependence, confirming theoretical predictions, and then focuses on the unexpected plateau in $T_c$ vs. $n_s$, interpreting it via resonance modes.
why_interesting: The study of melting transitions and correlated states in 2D electron systems is fundamental to understanding strongly correlated electron physics, which shares conceptual links with many-body dynamics in AMO systems.
